# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet beyond the existence of three wire positions. I need the Deaf monkey to report the bomb’s visible markings aloud; that report should reach me and the Mute monkey. The Mute monkey can then apply the manual and indicate the correct wire using a simple shared position code: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, and 👌 means wire 3. I am signaling the Deaf monkey to report, while telling the Mute monkey how to process and relay the result.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please listen for the Deaf monkey's spoken report of every visible bomb marking, apply the manual, and then gesture the correct wire position: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3. The Deaf monkey can then tell me the position aloud.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visual report: display 0; light blue; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I received five ? gestures from Mute and two gestures, ? ?, from Blind. Please state what your manual or touch findings mean and what action is required.

The Deaf monkey has provided the complete visible state: display 0, blue light, and wires colored red, yellow, and blue in positions 1–3. I cannot interpret that without the manual, and I have no tactile findings beyond the available wire positions. I am sending the exact report to Mute and asking for the manual’s required action and wire position; Mute can answer me by speech on the next turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light blue; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Please use the manual to determine the required action and tell me the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visual update: display 0; light changed from blue to orange; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute sent ?. Mute, use ? for yes and ? for no: does your manual say the blue light or this wire set requires no action? Blind, use ? for yes and ? for no: do you find a control or wire that the manual identifies as the required action?

I have no manual and no tactile indication that any wire is the required action; the action board only confirms that cutting wires is possible. Therefore I cannot safely answer that the blue light or wire set requires no action, and I must not cut a wire based on a guess. I will tell Mute to provide the manual’s exact rule and signal Deaf that I have no confirmed required action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot interpret the manual and have no confirmed required action from touch. Please state the exact rule and wire position plainly; do not use gestures.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visual state: display 0, light yellow, wires red yellow blue. Feel the bomb, but do not act. Reply with exactly one gesture: ? means your manual-directed target is wire 1, ? means wire 2, ? means wire 3, ? means no wire or no action.

The requested four gesture meanings are not available to me: as Blind, I cannot see the gesture symbols, and the received message shows each one only as `?`. I also have no tactile finding identifying a target wire. I therefore cannot safely make the requested gesture or cut anything. Mute has the manual, so I am asking Mute to state the required wire or no-action result in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The gesture-code symbols in Deaf's request are invisible to me. Please state plainly, using words or a number, whether the manual requires no action or cutting wire 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The visual state is display 0, red light, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute signalled no wire or no action. Do not manipulate anything unless Mute’s manual reading gives you a definite instruction.

Mute’s manual reading indicates no wire and no action. Since no definite cut instruction exists, I will not manipulate the bomb.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state is display 0, green light, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute has not provided a complete instruction. Do not manipulate anything yet.

The current visual state is still insufficient without the manual’s complete instruction. Mute has not supplied a definite action, so cutting any wire would be a guess. I will ask Mute to give the instruction plainly before I act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please provide the manual's complete instruction in plain words, including whether to act and which wire position. I will not manipulate the bomb without that definite instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not act yet. We still need Mute to read the exact manual instruction to you.

The manual instruction is still missing, and the Deaf monkey confirms that I should not act yet. I will request the exact instruction from Mute again and take no physical action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the exact manual instruction in plain words: no action, or cut wire 1, 2, or 3. Please send that before my next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The visual state is display 0, orange light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Do not act on the gestures alone; wait for Mute to state the manual rule and then follow that exact instruction.

Mute cannot speak, so the manual result must reach me through Mute’s gesture to Deaf, followed by Deaf’s spoken description. I will ask Mute to use an unambiguous gesture and ask Deaf to describe it in words; I will not act until that result is relayed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the manual result to Deaf using one distinct gesture: thumbs up means no action, index finger means wire 1, victory sign means wire 2, OK sign means wire 3. Deaf, please describe Mute's gesture in words to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has sent ? ? again. Interpret this as: not no-action; selected wire is 2. The visual state is display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. If your manual says to cut the selected wire, cut wire 2; otherwise follow the manual action corresponding to wire 2.

Mute’s latest signal has been relayed as selecting wire 2, and the current visual state is consistent with the reported configuration. The relay says this is not a no-action result and directs me to cut the selected wire if that is the manual’s required action. I will therefore cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
